call_sites: reckon/serve.py:1110 _CodeReload.finish calls route_results.stop_children before the exec that replaces the image
reckon/serve.py:3947 serve.main installs the SIGTERM unwind through _install_termination_unwind
reckon/serve.py:3999 serve.main's finally calls route_results.stop_children on the way out
reckon/serve.py:3896 _unwind_on_termination is the SIGTERM handler that raises SystemExit

0.reason: SIGTERM is the stop signal systemd and the test harness send, and SIGKILL cannot be caught; a hangup reaches a foreground server's whole process group, refresh children included, so no named stop path leaves a child running. The coordinator's population at d0709821f shows no teardown failure (0 against 4 before the repair).

findings.text: follow-on: the unwind is installed for SIGTERM alone, so a SIGHUP or SIGQUIT delivered to the served process still takes the interpreter down without running main's finally, and the refresh children the round exists to reap outlive it on that path; only SIGINT is covered for free, through the KeyboardInterrupt that reaches the same finally. The round brief states the requirement absolutely ('No refresh child may outlive the process that started it'), so the named SIGTERM-and-normal-exit paths are met and this is a gap against the stated property rather than against the named cases.

follow-on: the row asserting that the readiness-probe failure 'reproduces against an empty mount' rests on a startup figure (5.95 s with an empty mount, 5.2-7.4 s with the docs tree) that no log under the run's logs/ directory records; every other figure in the table resolves to a named log, so this row is an uncited measurement standing in for a receipt, and it is the load-independent half of the argument that the residual browser-probe failure is not this node's work.

follow-on: the supporting log closes with a bare 'EXIT=0' while all five runs it contains ended '1 failed', the exit status belonging to the concatenating wrapper rather than to any pytest invocation, so a reader who takes the log's last line for its verdict reads a pass that did not happen; the log also carries no header naming the revision or command it ran, which is why the one fact it supports (no 'Directory not empty' in any of the five) has to be read out of the body rather than the summary. The manifest annotates the figure as 'EXIT=0 overall', but the log itself does not.

follow-on: the test_logs value is written as semicolon-separated paths and prose on one line, and the audit's reader splits that field on ';' (reckon/crew/reports.py:1278), so the four entries it yields are fragments such as '.../gate-reap.log (run at 2483eeab1;' that resolve to no file; _read_control_log returns None for each (reckon/crew/reports.py:1124-1127) and the log-command check is skipped entirely. The hole is not visible, because check-manifest returns ok:true for this manifest for the same reason. Had the citations resolved, gate-reap.log would be flagged: its second line reads 'command PYTHONPATH=$PWD ...' with a space rather than the 'command:'/'cmd=' label _TEST_LOG_COMMAND_LABEL requires (reckon/crew/reports.py:1227), so the gate log names no extractable command. The gate is still reconstructable from the manifest's own tests: line and from after_suite, which parses as a dict carrying command, exit_status and log_path, so this does not invalidate the node's evidence - but a reader who trusts the clean check-manifest verdict has read an examination that never happened.
